Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) totally fun first (i.e., Entertainment game reappropriated), 
        (2) mostly fun first (i.e., design workshop with disabled stakeholders),
        (3) both fun and utility first (i.e., design workshop with diverse stakeholders), 
        (4) mostly utility first (i.e., primary utilitarian mechanic designed first),
        (5) totally utility first (i.e., made by clinicians or specialists, fun incorporated later)
reasoning: The system (VStroll) is explicitly designed to motivate walking and address utilitarian hurdles (poor infrastructure, monotonous walking) for people with visual impairments, focusing on exercise and spatial learning. It is presented as an accessibility/exercise technology rather than an entertainment game, with no indication of a fun-first or co-design-with-stakeholders entertainment focus. This aligns best with a mostly utility-first design where the primary utilitarian mechanic (exercise and navigation/spatial awareness support) is central, with engaging elements like virtual exploration added to reduce monotony.

        (1) unstructured play (i.e., no rules, making art),
        (2) semi-structured play (i.e., playground activities),
        (3) flexible structure with rules (i.e., improv),
        (4) flexible game (i.e., board game with house rules),
        (5) game with rigid rules (i.e., video game)
reasoning: The study centers on exergames and a smartphone app (VStroll) that use structured, rule-based interactions similar to video games and other exergames (e.g., VI-Tennis, Blind Hero, Pet-N-Punch, Eyes-Free Yoga). These are designed systems with defined goals, feedback, and constraints, fitting best with a game with rigid rules rather than open or loosely structured play.

Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely skill-based (i.e., trivia, sports),
        (2) mostly skill-based (i.e., mario kart),
        (3) equally skill and chance-based (i.e., catan),
        (4) mostly chance-based (i.e., Uno),
        (5) entirely chance-based (i.e., all dice)
reasoning: The study system (VStroll) is an audio-based virtual exploration app used while participants walk in real space. Outcomes depend on users’ walking, route choices, and navigation/spatial learning; there is no indication of random or chance-based mechanics. This makes the activity essentially skill- and behavior-based rather than involving probabilistic elements.

Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely solo (i.e., solitaire),
        (2) mostly solo (i.e., playing against AI in single-player StarCraft),
        (3) mix of solo and social affordances (i.e., animal crossing),
        (4) mostly social, but aspects are independent (i.e., house on hill haunt transition),
        (5) entirely social (i.e., tag)
reasoning: VStroll is described as an Android app used by individual participants walking alone in their own spaces while virtually exploring locations. There is no mention of multiplayer, co-present partners, or social interaction features; any future ideas (leaderboards, sharing) are only suggestions, not part of the studied design. Thus the studied design is entirely solo.

question:
Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely turn-based (i.e., tic tac toe),
        (2) follows a set of steps (i.e., viticulture's dynamic turn ordering),
        (3) turns are taken, but some actions can be taken at any time (i.e., pandemic),
        (4) most actions can be taken at any time, but there are some phases (i.e., PvP death reset timer),
        (5) entirely simultaneous (i.e., race)
reasoning: VStroll is a single-user virtual navigation/exploration app where the participant walks in real space while the system continuously provides spatial audio and step-count updates. There is no notion of alternating turns, phases, or restricted action windows; the user can walk and interact continuously. This best matches an entirely simultaneous design.

question:
Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely synchronous (i.e., real time strategy game),
        (2) mostly synchronous with a few asynchronous affordances (i.e., league of legends),
        (3) equal mix of synchronous and asynchronous affordances (i.e., helldivers 2),
        (4) mostly asynchronous with few synchronous affordances (i.e. cookie clicker),
        (5) entirely asynchronous (i.e., chess by postage mail)
reasoning: VStroll is a single-user virtual exploration and walking app with no mention of multiplayer, real-time interaction, or time-dependent coordination with others; all interactions (walking, route selection, POI discovery) are individually paced, fitting an entirely asynchronous design.

question:
Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely competitive (i.e., spit card game),
        (2) mostly competitive, but sometimes collaboration is important (i.e., forbidden island),
        (3) mix of competitive and collaborative (i.e., mario party 2 vs 2 mini-games),
        (4) mostly collaborative (i.e., animal crossing),
        (5) entirely collaborative (i.e., pandemic)
reasoning: The system (VStroll) is a single-user exergame-like walking app for people with visual impairments, focused on personal fitness, spatial learning, and self-set goals. There is no mention of multiple players, opponents, or any mechanics involving competition or cooperation between users; all described features (progress tracking, coaching, treasure-hunt-like POI discovery) are purely individual. Thus the design is entirely non-competitive and non-multiplayer, best matching an entirely collaborative/solo experience in this rubric.

Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely symmetrical (i.e., tic tac toe),
        (2) mostly symmetrical (i.e., undertale's differing NPC behaviors based on previous playthroughs),
        (3) both symmetrical and asymmetrical (i.e., pandemic with its similar turn structure but different character abilities),
        (4) mostly asymmetrical (i.e., tag),
        (5) entirely asymmetrical (i.e., keep talking, nobody explodes)
reasoning: The system (VStroll) is a single-user audio-based virtual exploration and exercise app with no distinct roles, teams, or differing abilities between players. All participants interact with the same interface and mechanics (walking while virtually exploring, receiving POI and fitness updates). There is no indication of asymmetric roles or capabilities, so the design is best characterized as entirely symmetrical.
